# Emaki

::: {.hero-lede}
Every coding-agent session on your machine, kept for good, in one window you
can also talk to.
:::

::: {.hero-sub}
A desktop app for Claude Code and Codex. It keeps every session byte for
byte, renders and searches all of them, and lets you carry one on from the
window.
:::

::: {.hero-cta}
[Download](install.qmd){.pill .pill-accent .i-download} [What's in it](features.qmd){.pill .i-scroll} [Source](https://github.com/alkaline-software/emaki){.pill .i-github}
:::

::: {.hero-meta}
For macOS, Windows and Linux. Open source, under the MIT licence.
:::

:::

::: {.band .rise}
## The thirty-day problem

Claude Code deletes its transcripts after thirty days, with no warning. Every
other tool in this space reads `~/.claude/projects` and stops there, so they
all inherit that expiry.

Emaki copies first and renders second. A session is in its archive from the
first time it is seen, so if anything else fails the bytes are already safe,
and one Claude Code has since deleted is still listed, still searchable,
marked *kept*.
:::

::: {.cards .rise}

::: {.card .i-archive}
### Kept for good
Every Claude Code session is copied byte for byte into `~/.emaki/archive`
before anything else touches it, and stays after Claude Code deletes it.
Codex keeps its own, so those are read in place.
:::

::: {.card .i-search}
### Search everything
[⌘K]{.kbd} searches every session you have ever run, a paragraph at a time,
live and kept together. [⌘F]{.kbd} finds inside the one you are reading.
:::

::: {.card .i-book-open}
### Read what it did
Prompts, replies, thoughts, tool calls and subagents, laid out like the
Claude app. Ask for one plain sentence on any tool call you cannot read.
:::

::: {.card .i-inbox}
### Carry on talking
Type to reply. A session running in a terminal gets the message through its
inbox; a finished one resumes under Emaki. Approvals, questions and plans
come up as cards.
:::

:::

::: {.band .rise}
## Beside the conversation

The window is built around the sessions, and what you reach for while
reading one sits at its side.
:::

::: {.cards .rise}

::: {.card .i-terminal}
### A terminal
A shell in the session's folder, or the agent's own screen as it runs,
two-way. Shells open in tabs.
:::

::: {.card .i-tree-view}
### The files
The project as a tree with git's marks. Open a file beside the conversation:
code, markdown, CSV, PDF, Word, slides, pictures. Edit it and save with
[⌘S]{.kbd}.
:::

::: {.card .i-git-branch}
### Git
Commit the files you tick, browse the history, switch and publish branches,
push and pull, without leaving the window.
:::

::: {.card .i-microphone}
### Dictation
On a Mac, talk instead of typing. A model downloaded to the machine writes it
down, Chinese and English mixed, and the shortcut works in any app.
:::

:::

::: {.band .rise}
## Nothing it will do to you

::: {.checks}
- **No hooks, ever.**
- Nothing writes to a transcript. The JSONL file is the only source of truth, and Emaki reads it.
- Nothing Emaki does enters a session's context window.
- Nothing is typed into a terminal of yours, and no terminal app is asked for anything. Emaki runs its own, hidden.
- No daemon and no browser. Everything lives in `~/.emaki`, and only `archive/` cannot be rebuilt: that is the one folder to back up.
:::

:::

::: {.band .rise}
## Built on the agents you already use

Emaki needs Claude Code or Codex installed and signed in. It adds three
things on top: conversations that never expire, one place to organize them,
and a readable view of what the agent did.

::: {.agents}

::: {.agent .agent-claude}
**Claude Code**

Read, search, keep and continue a session from the window, with its modes,
models and effort levels.
:::

::: {.agent .agent-codex}
**Codex**

Read, search, start, continue and stop, with approvals, questions and plans
on the same cards.
:::

:::
